title: Tenant proxy guard and regional swap playbook for Private/Dedicated control planes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-aware proxy guard and operational playbook that coordinates multi-region swap, circuit breakers, and load-shedding for Dedicated and Private control planes. The goal is to ensure predictable SLO preservation per-tenant during control-plane upgrades, region failover, and noisy-tenant incidents without bulk-impacting co-tenants. This includes: (1) a proxy-level admission controller that enforces per-tenant dynamic token buckets and soft/hard circuit thresholds, (2) an automated region-swap orchestration with canary routing and KV-cache warming/eviction policies, and (3) upgrade safety fencing that avoids cascading evictions during rolling control-plane upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy guard enforces per-tenant admission and rejects or queues excess requests according to dynamic policy at 95th percentile of observed load
Region-swap canary completes end-to-end with <500ms median additional latency for canary tenants and no data corruption in KV cache warming tests
During simulated noisy-tenant incident, non-impacted tenants remain above their configured availability SLOs (>= 99.5%) in the primary region
Rolling upgrade playbook prevents mass eviction: no more than 2% of active sessions evicted per tenant in upgrade window during staged rollout tests
Runbook and dashboards published; on-call can execute regional swap within defined 15 minute target and observe clear rollback path
steps: Design admission controller shim at edge proxy that consumes per-tenant policies from control plane; implement token-bucket + burst allowance + adaptive backoff
Define policy schema: soft_threshold_pct, hard_threshold_pct, degrade_action (queue|reject|route-to-secondary), kv_eviction_priority
Implement circuit-breaker telemetry hooks emitting tenant_id, route, reason, threshold, and action to Prometheus/OTel

Add region-swap orchestration component in control plane that sequences: prepare target region capacity, canary route subset of tenants, KV cache warm-up using snapshot+prefetch, switch routing, observe metrics, if healthy proceed to bulk swap
Add upgrade fencing gate: during control-plane upgrade set per-tenant safe-drain priority and temporarily disable aggressive eviction for tenants flagged as high-availability
Build automated chaos tests: noisy-tenant generator, slow-network, KV-cache corruption simulators to validate playbook
Create runbook pages and alert thresholds for SLO breaches and swap failures
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy enforcement logic and admission token accounting
Integration test: simulate 100 tenants with mixed qps, validate per-tenant metrics and circuit-breaker behavior
Staging canary: route 5% tenants to new region with KV warm-up; measure latency/throughput for 2 hours
Chaos run: introduce synthetic noisy tenant producing 10x normal QPS and validate isolation guarantees
Upgrade rehearsal: perform rolling control-plane upgrade with staging fencing enabled and assert eviction limits
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged deploy to staging control plane and edge proxies (QA signoff required)
Phase 1: Dark launch in production routing 1% of tenants through admission controller, collect telemetry for 72h
Phase 2: Canary region-swap tests with non-critical tenants (5% traffic) and manual verification
Phase 3: Incremental enablement for larger tenant segments with automated rollback on SLO regression
Phase 4: Full enablement and deprecation of previous ad-hoc eviction scripts

notes: Avoid large atomized evictions; prefer throttled queueing with backpressure to application clients where supported.
KV cache warm-up should prioritize top-n prefixes by recent access frequency to reduce cold-miss penalty during swap.
Consider fallbacks: if target region lacks capacity, fallback to degraded-mode in primary region instead of routing to a third region.
Plan for operator abort: include a clear abort criterion (increase in tenant error-rate > 2x baseline for 10m) and automated rollback steps.
